what_its_for: This medicine is used to relieve tension headaches that are hard to treat with regular pain relievers. It contains four ingredients that work together: butalbital relaxes muscle tension, aspirin reduces pain and inflammation, caffeine helps the other medicines work better, and codeine is a strong pain reliever.
how_to_take: Take this medicine exactly as your doctor tells you to. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. Do not crush, chew, or break the capsule. Do not take more than your doctor prescribed, and do not take it more often or for longer than directed. This medicine can be habit-forming, so only use it as needed.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 1 to 2 capsules every 4 hours as needed for pain. Do not take more than 6 capsules in one day (24 hours). Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different. Never increase your dose on your own.
missed_dose: This medicine is usually taken only when you have a headache, not on a regular schedule. If your doctor has told you to take it on a schedule and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in a safe place, locked up and out of reach of children and pets. Because it contains codeine, it is very dangerous for children. Dispose of any unused medicine properly — check with your pharmacist about drug take-back programs in your area.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Alcohol can increase your risk of serious side effects, including stomach bleeding and dangerous drowsiness. Avoid driving a car, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills, anxiety medicines, muscle relaxers, or other opioid pain medicines, without talking to your doctor first. Do not take other aspirin-containing or NSAID-containing products (like ibuprofen or naproxen) at the same time without checking with your doctor or pharmacist.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: difficulty breathing, very slow or shallow breathing, extreme drowsiness or difficulty waking up, confusion or unusual behavior, chest pain, coughing up blood or vomit that looks like coffee grounds, severe stomach pain or black/tarry stools, yellowing of your skin or eyes, fast or irregular heartbeat, seizures, signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or signs that you may be becoming dependent on the medicine, such as needing more of it to get the same effect or feeling like you cannot function without it.
when_it_works: This medicine usually starts to relieve headache pain within 30 to 60 minutes after taking it. It works best if you take it at the first sign of a headache, before the pain gets severe. The pain relief typically lasts about 4 to 6 hours.
special_populations: ELDERLY: Older adults are more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially dizziness, confusion, and breathing problems. Use with extra caution. PREGNANCY: This medicine should not be used during pregnancy, especially in the third trimester, as codeine and aspirin can harm the unborn baby and cause serious problems during delivery. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: Codeine passes into breast milk and can cause serious breathing problems in nursing infants. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. CHILDREN AND TEENAGERS: This medicine should NOT be given to children or teenagers, especially after surgery to remove tonsils or adenoids. Codeine is not safe for people under 18. Also, aspirin should never be given to children or teenagers due to the risk of a serious condition called Reye's syndrome. KIDNEY OR LIVER DISEASE: Use with caution if you have kidney or liver problems. Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine. HISTORY OF SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER: Because this medicine contains codeine and butalbital, both of which can be habit-forming, use with extreme caution if you or a family member has a history of drug or alcohol addiction.
